questions.text: What is a microtask in the event loop?
options: A job from the microtask queue: Promise.then, queueMicrotask, MutationObserver
Synchronous code still on the stack

questions.text: setTimeout(fn, 0) runs before Promise.resolve().then(fn).
What is the event loop?
questions.answer: The mechanism that pulls jobs from queues onto the call stack when the stack is empty. It drains the microtask queue first, then takes one macrotask (timer, I/O), then drains microtasks again.

questions.text: After synchronous code, in what order does the event loop run work?
options: Microtasks and macrotasks interleaved by enqueue time
Only macrotasks; microtasks wait for the next tick

questions.text: queueMicrotask puts the callback on the microtask queue.
How is a macrotask different from a microtask?
questions.answer: A macrotask (setTimeout, setInterval, I/O) is one turn of the “big” loop: after it finishes, the event loop drains every microtask. Microtasks (Promise.then, queueMicrotask) have higher priority and run back-to-back until that queue is empty.
